_note: A FICTIONAL business for testing tools/brand-discovery/build_brand_book.py. Not a client. Run: python3 tools/brand-discovery/build_brand_book.py --sample

answers.nameNotes: Short form “Nakheel”. In Arabic: محمصة نخيل
answers.markets: Muscat, with online orders across Oman
answers.oneLiner: We roast small batches of specialty coffee in Muscat and deliver it fresh to homes and offices.
answers.why: Most coffee here sits on shelves for months. We want people to taste coffee the week it was roasted, and to know where it comes from.
answers.vision: Two cafés in Muscat and a subscription that reaches every governorate.
answers.story:
It started in a garage in Al Khoud with a 1 kg roaster and a lot of burnt beans.

Friends kept asking for bags, then their offices did.
answers.values:
Freshness: we print the roast date on every bag.
Honesty: we tell you where each bean comes from.
Warmth: every customer is a guest.
answers.customer: Professionals aged 25–45 in Muscat who brew at home and care about quality. They follow coffee accounts on Instagram.
answers.problem: Supermarket coffee is stale and they can't tell where it came from.
answers.feel: Looked after, and a little proud of their taste
answers.trust: We roast to order and answer every WhatsApp message ourselves.
answers.notCustomer: People looking for the cheapest coffee by the kilo.
answers.compBad: Stale beans, no story, no service.
answers.different: The roast date is on every bag, and it reaches you within two days of roasting.
answers.person: A friendly barista who knows your order by name
answers.admire: Aesop, for its calm packaging. Muji, for keeping things simple.
answers.logoMessage: That we take coffee seriously, but we're warm and welcoming.
answers.avoid: Coffee cup clichés, coffee bean icons, steam swirls
answers.anything: We open the first café in March --> so the sign matters.
